Recursion is when a function solves a problem by calling itself on a smaller version of that same problem. Every recursive function needs a **base case** — a simple stopping condition that prevents it from calling itself forever. Each call does a little work, then passes a smaller problem down, until the base case is reached and the answers bubble back up. A classic example is `factorial(n) = n * factorial(n-1)`, which keeps multiplying downward until it hits `factorial(1) = 1` and returns.
